sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Behavioral interview questions are now equal-weighted with technical questions in every senior+ interview. This page covers the STAR method applied correctly, conflict resolution, agile/scrum scenarios, delivering under pressure, the failure-and-learning question (rehearsed but never canned), and career-growth narratives that do not sound rehearsed. For engineering-practice questions (code review, ADRs, technical debt, mentoring, technical leadership) see the Engineering Practices page — those are a separate, well-defined interview category.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Behavioural rounds use **STAR**: Situation → Task → Action → Result.

- **Situation** — set context in 2 sentences, no jargon.
- **Task** — what *you* owned (not the team).
- **Action** — concrete, in first person, ~3 specific moves.
- **Result** — measurable; quantify when you can.

Have **5 stories** ready that flex to: conflict, ambiguity, failure, leadership, technical depth.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **"Tell me about a failure"** — pick a real one, own your part, name the lesson.
- **"Difficult teammate"** — show empathy + structure; never trash-talk.
- **"Most challenging project"** — pick the *technically* hard one, not the politically hard one.
- **"Why this company"** — research; tie to their stack / scale / mission, not perks.
- **Avoid "we"** — interviewers want *your* contribution.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"Situation: <one-sentence context>. Task: <my specific responsibility>. Action: <three concrete moves>. Result: <quantified outcome + what I learned>."*
